wa_stamper_holland.notes: Stem the 6' wide chimney 40' before it narrows; clip a bolt at a constriction and traverse up-right 25' through broken ledges to a bolted belay midway across the face.
Traverse right another 25' to a short finger crack in the corner and build an anchor.
Climb the corner chimney system, passing a sandy ledge, then behind a large chockstone to a belay. Beware of potential rockfall.
Traverse right onto the Quarry Wall, passing 4 bolts before scrambling to the top. A pleasant, clean pitch.

wa_tpmv_10_meteorological_vinculation.notes: Shallow corners/cracks past 3 bolts and gear to anchor; usually climbed alone starting from Japanese Gardens P1. Continuing past this anchor adds a hard, height-dependent boulder section on small gear (5.12c/d), the route's crux. Continuing past that anchor through a hard, height-dependent boulder problem on small gear is the extended version and gives the route its 5.12c/d grade.
Slightly runout; cracks up right-facing corner to a ledge, then face climbing left to anchor below corner/slab pitch.
Slab-and-corner pitch; committing clip to first bolt, continues up difficult corner via bolts and gear.
Slab past bolts and gear with a tough mantle; multiple 5.8-5.9 finish variations.

wa_wild_wild_west.notes: Start at the first two bolts on a short prow at the lowest toe of the West Face. Climb the short opening face, then a series of fairly clean ramps and ribs to a belay on a good ledge. Extend a draw or two to keep rope drag down.
Follow bolts up a shallow groove left of the belay, traverse the right side of a small saddle to another bolt, then scramble up and left a short way to a good belay with chains.

Bolts lead up and right onto the exposed face; the crux is a slightly overhanging section about three-quarters of the way up. Ends at a semi-hanging belay on a small ledge. Can be linked with pitch 4 using alpine draws.
Clip a bolt up and left of the belay and step out onto the face with big exposure right away, then climb through a band of basalt to the top. Walk up and right to the true summit and its register.
